spark.scene: True-color satellite view of the main Hawaiian Islands with extensive white cumulus and cirrus clouds over dark ocean. The islands are partly to mostly obscured, with land only peeking through gaps, especially the large island in the southeast. No distinct gray, brown, or hazy streak distinguishable from ordinary meteorological clouds is visible; the summit area is covered by thick white clouds.

classify.caveats: No plume found; nothing to classify.

kilauea.activity_summary: The new vents stagnated last night, there is currently no active lava on the ground. The north, south, and west vents continue to glow. A minor summit deflation began at about 5 pm HST last night.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts increased in August, while the summit region showed no other signs of deformation. Mauna Loa had an increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 87 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the August reporting period, after 57 in July. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
